title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 5–7): Grothendieck builds a 'divided-power de Rham complex of the standard simplices' over an arbitrary base, aiming at commutative-type algebraic models for the cohomology of simplicial objects without inverting any primes. On the previous page, for a ring S, a PD-ideal J and an element t ∈ J, he sets C_DRpd[n](S,J,t) = (S⟨X_0..X_n⟩ / (ΣX_i − t)_pd) ⊗_S Λ*(S^{[n]}/diag). This is the PD de Rham complex of the PD-'simplex' ΣX_i = t, relative to S. As n varies it is a simplicial PD-dga with augmentation to S/J. He then evaluates it on simplicial objects: C(X_*) = Hom(X_*, C_*). In general this only gives a map to H*(X_*, S), not an isomorphism.

This page makes the universal choice. Take k a commutative ring, S = k⟨T⟩ (PD polynomial algebra in one variable), J = k⟨T⟩^+ (augmentation ideal) and t = T.

1. Eliminating T. Since T = ΣX_i and divided powers of T are forced, k⟨T,X_0..X_n⟩/(ΣX_i − T)_pd ≅ k⟨X_0..X_n⟩. Also S/J = k.

2. Simplicial modules. Let Φ_{k*} : [n] ↦ k^{[n]}. Read k^{[n]} as the k-valued functions on [n], i.e. the linear coordinate forms x_j. A map f:[m]→[n] pulls back x_j to Σ_{f(i)=j} y_i, so Φ_{k*} is a simplicial k-module. The constants (the diagonal, whose image is T = Σx_j) give k_* ⊂ Φ_{k*}. Set Ψ_{k*} = Φ_{k*}/k_* = [n] ↦ k^{[n]}/diag. Since the forms are relative to S, Σ dX_i = dT = 0, so the module of 1-forms is Ψ.

3. The boxed formula. Hence C**_DRpd*(k) := C_DRpd*(k⟨T⟩, k⟨T⟩^+, T) ≅ Γ_k(Φ_{k*}) ⊗_k Λ(Ψ_{k*}), as simplicial objects.

4. Structure. This is a bigraded object:
- p = PD-polynomial weight (the 'degré complémentaire');
- q = form degree;
- p+q = total degree.
It is a unital, associative, alternating (strictly anticommutative, odd squares zero) algebra, augmented to k. It carries divided powers on the augmentation ideal. The differential d(X^{[a]}) = X^{[a−1]} dX has bidegree (−1,+1), so it preserves total degree, and it is compatible with the PD structure.

What it serves (made explicit on p.7):
- Φ_* is the 0-coskeleton of k, hence contractible. So Γ^pΦ ⊗ Λ^qΨ is contractible for p ≠ 0.
- Each fixed total degree n gives a Koszul-type resolution 0 → k_* → Γ^nΦ → Γ^{n−1}Φ⊗Ψ → … → Λ^nΨ.
- All terms are acyclic except the last, and Λ^nΨ ≃ K(k,n) as a simplicial module (Ψ ≃ K(k,1), décalage).
- So Hom(X_*, weight-n part) computes H^q(X_*, k) for q ≤ n.

The point: inserting the PD variable T makes the PD-simplex homogeneous. The bigrading splits the PD-forms into weight pieces, each computing truncated integral cohomology. The PD algebra structure maps weight p ⊗ weight p' → weight p+p'. Comparing weights uses multiplication by T, and T·T^{[p]} = (p+1)T^{[p+1]} introduces factorials. That is presumably how this model coexists with the known obstruction to strictly commutative integral cochains: the obstruction is pushed into the weight grading.
errors: Minor: the arrow labelled 'réduction diagonale' between Φ_{k*} and k_* must, for Ψ = Φ/k_* to make sense simplicially, be the diagonal inclusion k_* → Φ_{k*} (constants; image of T). The sum map Φ → k is not simplicial. The arrow direction/label as transcribed is doubtful.
Notational: Φ_n = k^{[n]} is used both as the free module on [n] and as functions on [n]. Only the latter (contravariant) reading makes C_* simplicial, consistent with Hom(X_*, C_*).
The PD-ideal quotient by (ΣX_i − T)_pd identifies with k⟨X_0..X_n⟩ only because T is a PD variable. Correct as stated, but not justified on the page.

ideas.what: Homogenized PD-simplex: replace Σx_i = 1 by Σx_i = T with T a divided-power variable, so PD polynomial forms on simplices become bigraded (weight, form degree).
ideas.modern_name: Weight-graded (G_m-equivariant / Rees-type) divided-power polynomial de Rham forms on simplices
ideas.usually_credited_to: Polynomial forms on simplices: Sullivan (1977), H. Cartan (1976, rational/real). Integral or divided-power variants: later work (e.g. Cenkl–Porter, Karoubi) — unsure about exact precedence for the homogenized version.
ideas.where_published: Only in this unpublished 1976 IHÉS lecture material, as far as I know

ideas.what: Identification C_DRpd*(k⟨T⟩, k⟨T⟩^+, T) ≅ Γ_k(Φ_*) ⊗ Λ(Ψ_*) with Φ = functions on [n], Ψ = Φ/constants.
ideas.modern_name: PD Koszul / PD de Rham complex of a free module, applied levelwise to a simplicial module
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PD de Rham/Koszul complexes: Berthelot, Illusie (1970s)

ideas.what: Structure: bigraded, alternating, unital associative PD-algebra augmented to k, with differential of bidegree (−1,+1) compatible with divided powers.
ideas.modern_name: Bigraded (weight-graded) PD commutative dga / simplicial PD-cdga

ideas.what: (Prepared here, carried out on p.7.) Φ_* contractible, Ψ_* ≃ K(k,1), Λ^nΨ_* ≃ K(k,n); the weight-n part is a resolution of k_* computing cohomology truncated in degree ≤ n, for any base ring k.
ideas.modern_name: Integral de Rham theorem for divided-power simplicial forms, weight by weight
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (integral analogues of Sullivan's de Rham theorem appear in later literature)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's universal choice S = k⟨T⟩, t = T gives an integral, weight-graded divided-power commutative model of cochains. Each weight computes truncated cohomology, and weights are linked by multiplication by T with factorial defects. This is an early (1976) attempt at algebraic models of homotopy types over Z, predating Pursuing Stacks' 'schématisation'. It parallels much later work on integral cochain models (binomial rings: Horel, Kubrak–Shuklin–Zakharov; affine stacks: Toën) and on Rees/filtered-de Rham weight gradings. That link does not seem to be recorded.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a concrete PD-cdga, G_m-graded model in which the obstruction to strictly commutative integral cochains is absorbed into a weight grading. This could be compared with binomial-ring and affine-stack models of integral homotopy types.

missed.claim: The page sets up the bigraded structure but does not analyse how the different weights assemble: the system under multiplication by T, or a colimit/limit over weights. Nor does it determine which homotopy-theoretic information (e.g. Steenrod operations via divided powers) the multiplicative structure retains.
missed.quote: Structure : … bigraduée … à p.d. dans l'idéal d'augm. avec diff. de bidegré −1,+1 (donc degré total 0) compat. avec p.d.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Understanding the weight-transition maps would clarify whether this gives a genuinely new integral algebraic model of homotopy types or only a truncated, weight-wise one.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual ingredients (PD Koszul complexes, polynomial forms on simplices) are standard. The homogenizing trick (a PD variable T making the simplex graded, with each weight computing truncated integral cohomology) is a neat, apparently unpublished device. It belongs to Grothendieck's little-known 1976 IHÉS lecture on integral de Rham models. Notable as history, but likely partially rediscovered in spirit.
transcription_corrections: 'on prendra dominant' is probably 'on prendra donc maintenant' or similar.
The arrow 'réduction diagonale' most likely reads 'inclusion diagonale' (k_* → Φ_{k*}).
'où k.a.' is likely 'et p.d.' (à puissances divisées dans l'idéal d'augmentation).

Left margin likely says the bigraduation is compatible with ('vérifie') the structures of S, and that divided powers are given on the augmentation ideal ('ici de degré 2' refers to bidegree considerations).
On the next page, 'cycliques' should read 'acycliques'.
